business_scope.primary_industry_name: Offshore Trade Intermediary and Commercial Re-Invoicing Operations

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Civil Law (private law, Civil Code of Québec) and Common Law (federal public and criminal law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and its Regulations; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, Part XII.2; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2; Civil Code of Québec, articles 2202-2241 (limited partnership formation and governance); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR, c. P-44.1, particularly sections 10, 14, 35-40; Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, RRQ, c. P-44.1, r. 3; Order in Council implementing Quebec's registrant disclosure rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of Corporate General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Authorized corporate registry in the General Partner's jurisdiction of formation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Board Resolutions of Corporate General Partner Authorizing Formation of the Limited Partnership
Power of Attorney Appointing Local Agent / Authorized Representative in Québec
Beneficial Ownership Identification Statements and UBO Declaration Schedule
Certified True Copies of Passport / National Identity Documents of Signatories and UBOs

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, partners, authorized representatives, and signatories against: (1) Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List and Domestic Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act; (2) Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) Guidance 71 concerning politically exposed persons (PEPs) and heads of international organizations, with domestic PEPs treated as high-risk; (3) United Nations Security Council Consolidated Lists; (4) United States Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List and OFAC sanctions programs; and (5) Her Majesty's Treasury UK Sanctions List where applicable. Any positive match or reasonable suspicion must be escalated immediately to the AML Compliance Officer for enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and, where required, filing of a suspicious transaction report with FINTRAC.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Registre des entreprises (online services: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Pursuant to the Charter of the French Language, CQLR, c. C-11, any business designation used in Québec must have a French version. A name that is exclusively in English is generally forbidden. The French version of the name must be employed in all legal documents, contracts, and signage. Non-Latin-script names must first be transliterated into Latin characters; where phonetically applicable, the Registraire requires a French transliteration to ensure the name can be pronounced and read by a francophone. The Registraire assesses risk of confusion on the basis of transliterated forms and also reviews the descriptive and distinctive elements of the proposed name for compliance with public order and bona fide commercial usage.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file a 'demande de révision' (request for review) with the Registraire des entreprises within 15 days of the date of the refusal. The request must contain written legal and factual grounds, including evidence of distinctiveness, prior consent of any affected party, or the availability of disclaimers. The Registraire is obliged to reconsider the application and issue a written decision without undue delay. If the second review is also refused, the applicant may, within 30 days of the revised decision, apply to the Court of Québec for judicial review under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR, c. P-44.1, section 42, or seek an alternative name for reservation. The applicant may also petition the Commission de toponymie for authorization where the refusal involves a toponymic or official geographic element.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is generally permissible for administrative and postal correspondence, provided that the registered office is a physical address in Québec where service of process, legal notices, and statutory records may be delivered. For the general re-invoicing trade sector, the Registraire des entreprises and the Agence du revenu du Québec (ARQ) routinely reject a 'virtual' registered office that is merely a post-office box or a shared desk without a designated and authorized person present during business hours. If the virtual office provides a reception desk, accepts official correspondence, maintains a register of documents, and is staffed during at least 40 business hours per week, it is typically accepted. The applicant should engage a local service provider approved for 'commercial domiciliation.'
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-Enhanced: approximately 25% annual probability of an unannounced inspection of the registered office and/or books and records by the Registraire des entreprises or the Agence du revenu du Québec. The probability rises to 40% where the limited partnership operates as a pass-through re-invoicing hub with no local employees, a virtual registered office, and high-volume intercompany transactions. Conversely, the risk falls to below 10% where the entity maintains a physical office, a designated local manager, and audited financial statements demonstrating commercial substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c. CCQ), arts. 2246–2266 (société en commandite / limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1), ss. 1–30, 94–105.1; Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1, r. 3); Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.), s. 96 governs federal pass-through taxation. The Canada Business Corporations Act does not apply to a Quebec limited partnership.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar) — the official state registry for legal publicity of enterprises, accessible through the 'Espace entrepreneurs' e-filing portal under the Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation — Déclaration de société en commandite (Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership), e-filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and evidenced by the Certificat d'attestation (attestation of registration) and the 10-digit Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Quebec limited partnership; capital is fixed solely by the partnership agreement (contrat de société), and contributions may be money, property, or services. No escrow or capital deposit is mandated. First-year state fees total approximately CAD 126 (CAD 33 registration fee plus CAD 93 annual fee), equivalent to about USD 92.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST WRITTEN RESOLUTIONS OF THE GENERAL PARTNER. RESOLVED: (1) The General Partner accepts the capital subscriptions of the initial limited partners in the amounts set out in the Partnership Agreement, and acknowledges receipt of all contributions made to date. (2) The registered office of the Partnership is established at [Service Address], Montreal, Quebec, and the General Partner is directed to file the declaration of registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. (3) [Full Name] is appointed managing representative of the Partnership, with sole authority to open and operate bank accounts, sign SWIFT/TT/LC payment instructions, and effect all statutory filings. (4) All applicable registration fees are approved for payment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Common-Law Trademark Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — online name search module ('Recherche de noms'); Canadian Intellectual Property Office (CIPO) Canadian Trademarks Database
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a name search on the Registraire's public module to verify that the proposed partnership name is not identical or confusingly similar to existing legal persons, partnerships, or sole proprietorships registered in Quebec. Confirm that the name includes the mandatory identifying expression 'société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.'. Perform a complementary CIPO trademark search to avoid infringement of federal trademarks. Document the results in a counsel memorandum.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire later refuses the name on confusion grounds during declaration review, the applicant must amend the name and refile the declaration; the refused name search does not block a resubmission, and no separate name-reservation fee is lost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement (Contrat de Société en Commandite)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notarial office (mandatory only if a partner contributes a Quebec immovable) and external transactional legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the partnership agreement under Civil Code of Québec arts. 2246–2262, specifying the firm name, registered office in Quebec, object (offshore trade intermediary and commercial re-invoicing operations, NAICS 425120 / ISIC 4690), identity of the general partner (commandité), schedule of limited partners (commanditaires), capital commitments, profit-sharing ratios, and management authority of the general partner. All partners must sign; notarization is required only for contributions comprising Quebec immovables.
required_dossiers: Identification and proof of address for each partner
Powers of attorney if signing by representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: This is a private contractual step, not a government filing; any defect is cured by re-execution or by an amendment agreement signed by all partners before the declaration of registration is submitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Declaration of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — 'Espace entrepreneurs' e-filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online 'Déclaration d'immatriculation (société en commandite)': enter the partnership name, registered office address in Quebec, mailing address, general partner identification and address, activity description with SCIAN/NAICS code 425120, commencement date, and a statement that the enterprise is a civil-law limited partnership regulated by the Civil Code of Québec. Transmit the declaration electronically, pay the CAD 33 registration fee plus CAD 93 annual fee by credit card or Interac, and save the system acknowledgment with the assigned filing number.
required_dossiers: Partnership agreement digest (name, registered office, object)
Lease, deed, or occupancy authorization for the registered office in Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire issues a notice of non-compliance or requests amended particulars, rectify the declared information and resubmit within 30 days through the same portal; unpaid or declined fees are completed via the 'pending filings' queue without recommencing the entire application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the Attestation of Registration and Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (automated issuance upon approval)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, download the Certificat d'attestation (attestation of the declaration of registration) from the Espace entrepreneurs account. Record the 10-digit NEQ and the registration date. Verify that the legal name, object, registered office, and general partner details match the authorized partnership documents; the attestation constitutes the official proof of formation for banking and contracting counterparties.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the attestation is not generated or contains registry errors, contact the Registraire's correction service through the online dossier; administrative rectification and reissuance are effected without additional fee when the error is attributable to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Business Number and GST/QST Tax Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency — Business Registration Online (BRO); Revenu Québec — 'Mon dossier d'entreprise'
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NEQ and attestation, register the limited partnership with CRA Business Registration Online to obtain the 9-digit federal Business Number (BN), activating the RT (GST/HST) and RP (payroll) program accounts as needed. Open the Quebec QST account with Revenu Québec through the enterprise file, mirroring the GST registration, because the partnership is deemed a registrant for QST purposes when GST registration applies. Register the employer file with the CNESST if employees will be engaged.
required_dossiers: CRA form RC160 (GST/HST) and Revenu Québec QST application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or Revenu Québec requests clarifications, respond within 30 days via the business account portal; misstated particulars are corrected online and the BN or QST number is activated retroactively to the registration date once the information is reconciled.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Payment Rail Configuration (SWIFT/LC/TT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Schedule I Canadian chartered banks (e.g., National Bank of Canada, RBC, TD, BMO) — commercial banking and KYC compliance teams
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Certificat d'attestation, NEQ, partnership agreement, and general partner KYC documentation to open a partnership current account in the LP's name capable of SWIFT wire receipts and outbound transfers. Submit the bank's due diligence pack, beneficial ownership confirmation, and expected transaction profile for the re-invoicing hub, which is classified under the bank's Medium-Risk Enhanced AML tier. If trade finance is required, apply for a documentary credit (LC) facility linked to the partnership's purchase and re-sale invoices.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the partnership agreement
General partner passport/ID and proof of address
Bank AML questionnaire describing re-invoicing payment flows and counterparty jurisdictions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide notarized identification, registry extracts, and sample underlying trade contracts; escalate to the bank's KYC compliance officer, or if the account is declined, apply at another regulated financial institution and supplement the package with the corrected AML narrative.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 4690 wholesale trade intermediary and commercial re-invoicing is a non-manufacturing activity; the sole registration authority is the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, and no industrial licensing board is triggered. Sectoral permits (e.g., Revenu Québec/Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux) would apply only upon future diversification into regulated goods.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None mandatory. The operational authorization is the Certificat d'attestation d'immatriculation (Quebec enterprise registration attestation) together with the federal GST/HST and Quebec QST accounts. No municipal trade license is required for office-based re-invoicing operations in most Quebec municipalities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Exempt — registration only. Pure commercial re-invoicing generates no environmental discharges, and no full EIA or authorization under s. 22 of the Environmental Quality Act (CQLR c. Q-2) is required. If warehousing or logistics capacity is added later, the project would be re-assessed under the Regulation respecting the declaration of certain substances and discharges (REAFIE).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or residual-material thresholds apply to an office-only re-invoicing operation. The general duty to avoid contamination under s. 20 of the Environmental Quality Act remains binding. Any future warehousing must comply with the Regulation respecting the landfilling and incineration of residual materials (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 19) and any applicable REAFIE reporting thresholds for air and water discharges.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Standard municipal fire prevention inspection certificate for the office premises (e.g., Service de prévention des incendies de Montréal for a Montreal registered office); compliance with Chapter I of the Quebec Building Code governing structural loads, means of egress, and fire separations for the leased space; registration of the employer with the CNESST through the employer declaration if staff are hired, together with the mandatory orientation and training program prescribed by the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c. S-2.1). No special physical clearance applies to a pure re-invoicing operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – GST/HST and federal income tax administration; Revenu Québec – Quebec Sales Tax (QST), provincial corporate income tax, and payroll duties. Portals: CRA My Business Account; Revenu Québec CLIENT (Services en ligne des entreprises).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident limited partnership carrying on business in Canada must obtain a CRA Business Number (BN) and register for GST/HST where required, using Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or online via CRA My Business Account. For Quebec nexus, the partnership must also register with Revenu Québec through the Registrant Registration Service (formerly Form LM-1) to obtain a QST registration and separate QST number. The LP must appoint a resident agent for service of process when no permanent establishment exists, and provide partnership identification including all general and limited partners. The BN/GST/HST registration must be completed before commencing commercial activity in Canada or within one month after reaching the taxable-supply threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box election; limited partnerships are fiscally transparent under the Income Tax Act. The partnership must file an information return (Form T5013) allocating income/loss to partners. Non-resident partners may elect under the Income Tax Act s.216 to file a return for Canadian-source rental or timber income, but for trading income the standard withholding regime applies. For GST/HST, the partnership or a designated member may elect to register as a group or as a participating partnership under s.178 of the Excise Tax Act. In Quebec, the registrant may elect with a partner to make that partner the QST registrant for the partnership's activities under the Taxation Act (Quebec). Hybrid mismatch elections under Canadian tax law are not available as a distinct election, but treaty-based and applicable domestic allocation rules may mitigate double taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax for GST; Quebec Sales Tax for QST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies over a single calendar quarter or across four consecutive calendar quarters (for both GST/HST and QST small-supplier rules; non-residents may be required to register earlier if carrying on business in Canada).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not mandate continuous transaction controls, real-time tax clearance, or digital stamping. Electronic invoicing is permitted and encouraged via the Pan-Canadian Peppol network (CanBII) for B2B transactions. Businesses must issue compliant invoices under the Excise Tax Act and the Quebec Taxation Act, but no government API clearance is mandatory. A re-invoicing hub must retain all electronic records in Canada or make them available electronically to CRA/Revenu Québec upon audit; failure to provide e-records on request may lead to assessment.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of tangible personal property that are exported from Canada in accordance with the Excise Tax Act Schedule IX Part V ss.16-20 and, for Quebec, the QST system mirroring GST export rules. For general re-invoicing trade where the intermediary never takes possession or the buyer is a non-resident and goods are shipped directly from a foreign supplier to a foreign buyer, the Canadian LP must establish that the supply is made to a non-resident and the property is not delivered or made available in Canada. Offshore services supplied to non-residents concerning goods located outside Canada may also be zero-rated under Schedule IX Part V s.7. To claim zero-rating the LP must hold contemporaneous evidence confirming the direct export, including shipping instructions, commercial terms, and transfer of ownership abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Invoice or commercial invoice indicating zero-rated supply
Form B13A – Canada Customs Export Declaration or approved CAED electronic equivalent
Transport document (Bill of Lading, air waybill, or truck manifest)
Proof of export from Canadian territory (carrier certificate, customs stamp, outward presentation notice)
Foreign exchange record and inward remittance certificate or bank transfer confirmation proving payment from the non-resident buyer
Controller/provincial QST and federal GST/HST remission documentation, if applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec aggressively review zero-export claims. A taxpayer who cannot substantiate physical export or the foreign destination will be reassessed to collect uncollected GST/HST or QST, with interest retroactive from the reporting period. For knowing or grossly negligent misrepresentations, penalties of 50% of the tax avoided under the Excise Tax Act s.285 and Taxation Act provisions, plus criminal prosecution under the Criminal Code, can apply. The normal reassessment period is four years for GST/HST and, for income matters involving non-arm's length partners, seven years; the period is unlimited where fraud or misrepresentation is proven. A re-invoicing structure that lacks economic substance may also be challenged under GAAR, leading to full clawback of zero-rating benefits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as monetary authority; prudential regulation by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) under the Bank Act (S.C. 1991, c. 46); AML/CFT supervision by FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA); retail payment system oversight under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA). Canada maintains no dedicated foreign-exchange control agency; the Minister of Finance retains residual approval powers only under the Investment Canada Act for foreign investment, not for FX flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible under IMF Article VIII. Canada imposes no exchange controls on current-account transactions (trade in goods and services, dividends, interest, partner distributions) or capital-account transactions (FDI, shareholder loans, loan repayments, liquidation proceeds). The Quebec Limited Partnership may freely receive capital contributions, invoice foreign customers, and repatriate profits to non-resident partners without Bank of Canada approval or declaration. Practical constraints are limited to (i) FINTRAC reporting of international electronic fund transfers (IEFTs) of C$10,000 or more by the financial institution, (ii) OSFI Guideline B-8 enhanced due diligence on non-resident-owned entities, and (iii) Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act on payments to non-residents, subject to treaty relief — a tax matter, not a convertibility restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada has no export-proceeds surrender regime, no statutory repatriation timeline, and no mandatory conversion ratio. The Quebec LP may hold, invest, and disburse USD, EUR, or other foreign currency proceeds freely in domestic or offshore accounts. Applicable obligations are limited to (i) accurate invoicing, transfer-pricing documentation, and customs valuation with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for goods physically crossing the border; and (ii) bank record-keeping and FINTRAC EFT reporting obligations. Where re-invoicing involves direct shipment from a third-country supplier to the end customer without entry into Canada, the transactions fall outside CBSA scope but still require full documentary support to satisfy bank AML/KYC review.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
Desjardins (Fédération des caisses Desjardins du Québec)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for primary treasury use. Offshore fintech EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Currencycloud, Payoneer) operate in Canada as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) registered with FINTRAC rather than as chartered banks; balances are not CDIC-insured and the EMI is not a direct SWIFT member. Since 2024, payment service providers must additionally register under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) with the Bank of Canada. A Quebec LP may use an EMI for ancillary receivables collection or FX conversion, but the main liquidity and clearing rail should be a Tier-1 Canadian bank account to obtain direct SWIFT membership, documentary LC capability, and an auditable trail for the re-invoicing model. Inbound transfers routed from an unregulated offshore EMI into a domestic bank account will trigger enhanced due diligence and may be placed on hold pending full commercial invoice documentation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is available at most Tier-1 banks, but always subject to a mandatory live video or telephonic compliance interview; a purely digital, no-human-opening flow is rarely granted for a non-resident-owned Limited Partnership. The General Partner's authorized directors and the LP's ultimate beneficial owners (25% or more) may be asked to attend an in-person meeting with a compliance officer at a Montreal or Toronto branch, unless the bank accepts notarized identity verification packages. For a Quebec LP, the bank requires: (i) the Certificate of Registration and Declaration of Registration issued by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ); (ii) the notarized or written limited partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite); (iii) the GP's certificate of incorporation, articles, by-laws, director register, and incumbency certificate; (iv) UBO declarations for all partners; and (v) a certified French or English translation of any foreign-issued documents. Silent limited partners need not appear physically, but their full KYC packages must be disclosed and verified.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Triangulation trade pattern: the re-invoicing LP invoices goods it never physically receives or ships, creating a mismatch between invoice counterparties and transport documents (bill of lading, airway bill, customs entry).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a complete documentary chain: end-buyer purchase order; supplier proforma invoice and final commercial invoice; intercompany re-invoicing and trading services agreement; forwarder booking confirmation; original bill of lading or airway bill; packing list; shipping instruction evidencing direct seller-to-buyer delivery; applicable CBSA import/export declarations; and a board-approved commercial rationale memorandum explaining margin structure, risk allocation, and the economic substance of the Quebec LP.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through and factoring red flags: high volume of round-sum wires, rapid in-and-out transaction velocity, payments to third parties not named on the invoice, and mismatched purpose codes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Adopt and furnish a treasury control framework: monthly cash-flow forecast; sub-limits on same-day in/out flows; dual-authorization transaction approvals; invoice-to-PO-to-delivery matching protocol; standing instruction prohibiting free-text narratives on MT103 fields except structured purpose codes; and a quarterly external CPA review of treasury operations. Provide the bank a written undertaking to produce supporting trade documents for any sampled transaction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident partner opacity: multi-tier overseas limited partners obscure the ultimate beneficial owner determination (Canada applies a 25% ownership threshold) and trigger OSFI B-8 enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the full partner register with each partner's legal name and jurisdiction; a UBO organizational chart traced to natural persons; the GP's certificate of good standing; GP board resolution authorizing the account opening and confirming signatory authority; trust deed and trust register for any trust partner; corporate registry extracts for any corporate partner; and signed Canadian tax-residency declarations for all partners, together with Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) registration confirmation where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk counterparty exposure: suppliers or customers located in sanctioned or AML-flagged jurisdictions (OFAC/OSFI restricted states, FATF grey-listed jurisdictions), or repeatedly screening positive in adverse media.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare an independent sanctions and adverse-media screening report covering all counterparties; provide Global Affairs Canada export permit determinations and, where relevant, CBSA import/export controls clearance letters; confirm no dealings with OFAC/OSFI-listed entities; append a sanctions-compliance clause from each master supply agreement; and deliver KYC files for every material counterparty consisting of certificate of incorporation, registry extract, and UBO list.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route inbound partner capital via SWIFT MT103 (customer transfer) or MT202 (bank-to-bank for nostro repositioning) to the LP's designated operational account held at the Canadian Tier-1 bank. Beneficiary name must exactly match the LP's registered legal name under REQ. Remittance Information (field 70) should read 'Partner Capital Contribution — [Partner Name] — [Date]'; for intercompany loans, use 'Shareholder Loan — [Agreement Ref]' and attach the loan agreement. Canadian banks automatically report all international transfers of C$10,000 or more to FINTRAC as IEFTs; this is a reporting obligation, not an approval gate. To avoid delays, deliver to the bank in advance: the partnership agreement, the GP board resolution authorizing the capital call, source-of-wealth documentation for each contributing partner, and a statement of the contribution's commercial purpose (working capital for trade settlements, LC collateral cover, or operating expenses). Avoid generic purpose codes such as 'fees' or 'services' that do not match the underlying trade flow.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct telegraphic transfers to suppliers and end-customers, using structured remittance data referencing invoice numbers and purchase order numbers; (2) Commercial documentary Letters of Credit issued via SWIFT MT700 from the Quebec LP's bank in favor of suppliers, governed by UCP600, payable at sight or by acceptance; (3) MT202 for interbank repositioning to cover LC reimbursement claims under URC522 where documentary collections are used; (4) domestic CAD payments via the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or Real-Time Rail (RTR) for Quebec operating expenses. The LP should operate a payment factory from a master operational account with segregated CAD, USD, and EUR sub-accounts, executing FX conversions only at settlement time under the bank's electronic banking portal. Every outward payment must be matched to the trade document package (invoice, PO, proof of delivery, customs entry) to avoid FINTRAC suspicious transaction reporting and to preserve transfer-pricing defensibility.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/CAD deliverable outright forwards (standard onshore market, maturities up to 24 months, offered by all Tier-1 Canadian banks without complex ISDA documentation for plain-vanilla tenors)
USD/CAD FX swaps (spot-forward and forward-forward combinations) for managing rolling settlement liquidity
Cross-currency swaps (USD/CAD, EUR/USD, USD/CNH) for matched long-dated invoice and payable cycles under ISDA/CSA master agreements
Vanilla FX options (USD/CAD calls and puts) for contingent or bi-laterally uncertain trade flows

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for third-country non-convertible legs (e.g., USD/CNY, USD/INR, USD/BRL) executed with offshore counterparties; CAD NDFs are neither offered nor necessary because the CAD/USD onshore deliverable market is fully functional
Money-market forward-rate agreements and swap-point trading against LVTS and correspondent balances for short-term liquidity optimization
Foreign-currency deposit sweeps and multi-currency notional pooling to reduce idle currency risk across the CAD/USD/EUR account structure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after the annual anniversary of the registration of the limited partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The REQ issues a notice of default followed by an administrative delay penalty; continued failure exposes the registration to administrative cancellation after a cure notice. A cancelled registration loses third-party opposability and may expose limited partners to general-partner liability for obligations arising after cancellation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Partnership Information Return (T5013) and partner slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the partnership fiscal period-end; for a December 31 year-end, the filing deadline is June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file attracts late-filing penalties and daily arrears interest under the Income Tax Act; repeated willful non-filing may lead to prosecution and disallowance of partnership expense deductions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Partnership Information Return (CO-17) and Relevé RL-15 slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal period-end, no later than March 31 of the following calendar year; non-calendar fiscal periods follow the corresponding statutory due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Revenu Québec imposes interest and late-filing penalties on unpaid obligations; deficient RL-15 or CO-17 filings can trigger matching-assessment adjustments against partners and administrative garnishment of provincial refunds.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual internal register audit memorandum for the limited partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Maintained at the partnership principal establishment; not filed with a government authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed and dated no later than 90 days after the partnership fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government filing penalty; an incomplete register audit trail exposes the general partner to fiduciary liability and weakens the enforceability of partner indemnification provisions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No Quebec or federal statutory audit threshold applies solely by reason of limited partnership status. An audit becomes compulsory only when required by the partnership agreement, lender covenants, a court order, or securities law classification as an investment fund or reporting issuer. A privately held re-invoicing intermediary LP with no public offering will normally have no statutory audit mandate.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted under the CPA Canada Handbook Part I, or Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) under Part II. ASPE is the customary framework for a private limited partnership; consolidation and tax allocation follow the partnership agreement and applicable Canadian tax rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual beneficial-ownership confirmation is filed for Quebec limited partnerships. The Quebec annual declaration updates only registration particulars such as the limited partnership name, head office, place of business, object, and general partner identity. Transfers of limited partnership interests are recorded internally in the partnership ledger; a registered amendment is required only if the transfer changes the sole general partner or other registration particulars. Canada's federal corporate beneficial-ownership registry does not apply to partnerships.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members — maintained as the limited partners' ledger for capital accounts and interest transfers
Register of Directors / General Partners — maintained at the principal establishment for manager appointments and changes in general partner identity
Minute Book — annual and extraordinary resolutions of the general partner, meeting minutes, and capital transaction approvals

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 – 900 per year for registered office and local agent services in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No compulsory statutory audit; voluntary financial statement preparation or review typically USD 2,500 – 7,500, with a full certified audit estimated at USD 8,000 – 18,000 if required by a lender or investor

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined for corporate partners (federal 15% general corporate rate + Quebec 11.5% general corporate rate); the Limited Partnership itself is fiscally transparent and not a taxable entity.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory corporate tax holiday applies to a limited partnership. Available preferences include: federal small business deduction for Canadian-controlled private corporation partners (federal 9% + Quebec 3.2% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income); SR&ED investment tax credits; Quebec innovation and R&D tax credits; capital cost allowance deductions; and Quebec resource-related deductions. For Canadian-source business income allocated to non-resident partners, Part I tax applies at the partner level absent treaty relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return (Federal): filed via CRA My Business Account or approved Efile/T5013 software; accompanied by T5013 Summary and T5013 slips for each partner.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before five months after the partnership's fiscal period-end (e.g., May 31 for a December 31 year-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Business Number (BN), RC account identifier, mailing address, and fiscal period of the partnership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the Canadian agent or representative's contact information and expressly identify any non-resident partners and their tax treaty residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Date on which the partnership year ends; the same fiscal period must apply to all partners and may not exceed 12 months unless CRA approval is obtained.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the period stated in the partnership agreement; for non-resident partners, ensure the period is consistently reflected in their home-jurisdiction filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 — Net income or loss from business
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting profit to taxable income, including adjustments for non-deductible expenses, capital cost allowance, and Canada-source business income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only business income attributable to Canada through the partnership's permanent establishment in Quebec; a re-invoicing hub must report the arm's-length margin without inflated intercompany charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, Business Number, share ratio, partner type, and allocated income/loss for each partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate Canadian-source business income to non-resident limited partners and require them to file a Canadian Part I return unless a treaty exemption applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under Income Tax Act s.162(7.1): CAD 100 per month per partner (maximum 12 months), plus prescribed interest on unremitted amounts; gross negligence penalties of 50% of understated tax for knowingly incomplete or false information.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: TP-600 Information Return for a Partnership (Quebec): filed through Revenu Quebec's 'clic Revenu' online portal; accompanied by Relevé 15 slips for Quebec-resident partners.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within five months after the partnership's fiscal year-end (e.g., May 31 for a December 31 year-end); quarterly instalments may apply for corporate partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) from the Registraire des entreprises, Revenu Quebec account ID, and mailing address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the general partner is a non-resident corporation, designate a Canadian agent for service and provide its Quebec business address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2 — Business income attributable to Quebec
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income or loss derived from carrying on business in Quebec through a permanent establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate to Quebec only assets, functions, and risks physically located in Quebec; invoice-only activity without an actual place of business may not create Quebec nexus for income tax purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Each partner's share of income/loss, source deductions, and previous-year loss carryovers applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must certify residence and provide treaty certificates where reduced withholding is claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total of Relevé 15 slips issued to partners must equal the TP-600 allocations and the federal T5013 allocations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners without Canadian residency, issue Relevé 15 only to the extent the allocation is attributable to Quebec; otherwise record the amount as a non-resident remittance item.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under the Quebec Tax Administration Act: CAD 100 per month per partner up to CAD 2,500 for late filing; false statements penalty of 50% of understated tax; criminal prosecution may result in fines up to CAD 100,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Income Tax Act Part XIII on taxable dividends paid by a Canadian corporation to a non-resident person (portfolio rate). For the Quebec Limited Partnership itself, profit distributions are not dividends; they are allocated partnership income taxed under Part I. If the LP is used with a Canadian corporate vehicle, any dividend distribution from that vehicle attracts 25% statutory withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief for reduced withholding, the non-resident beneficial owner must complete and deliver Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits under a Tax Convention) to the Canadian payer before payment, together with an official tax residency certificate (for U.S. taxpayers, IRS Form 6166; for other treaty jurisdictions, the equivalent certificate issued by the competent authority). The payer must retain the documentation in its books. The Quebec-specific form TP-1016 applies for Quebec deductions but does not replace federal NR301 for income tax treaty purposes. If documentation is incomplete, withhold at the statutory 25% and remit; a refund may be claimed on Form NR7 within two years of the end of the calendar year in which the amount was paid.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25% under Part XIII; treaty rates generally 10% for most royalties under Canada-U.S. DTA, with 0% for computer software and certain intellectual property rights. Interest: statutory 25% under Part XIII; arm's-length interest to non-residents is exempt under s.212(1)(b)(vii), and most DTA including Canada-U.S. provide 0% to 15% source state taxation. A re-invoicing hub must isolate royalties or embedded financing income from the sale invoice to avoid recharacterization as a management fee or dividend.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No fixed statutory monetary threshold for preparing contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation; however, CRA penalty-safe-harbour thresholds are CAD 1,000,000 for cross-border goods and services transactions and CAD 50,000 for guarantee fees. Country-by-country reporting is mandatory for Canadian ultimate parent entities with consolidated group revenue equivalent to EUR 750,000,000 or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada and Quebec do not impose UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the Income Tax Act's General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s.245) and transfer-pricing standard (s.247) apply substance-over-form and commercial rationality tests. A re-invoicing LP that lacks employees, premises, business assets, or meaningful decision-making functions will be disregarded for lack of economic substance, and its profit allocations may be re-allocated to the parties that actually perform functions and bear risks.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully evading tax by maintaining fictitious re-invoicing records, suppressing sales, fabricating purchase invoices, or making false statements in T5013/TP-600 filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: On summary conviction under Income Tax Act s.239: fine of 50% to 200% of tax evaded and imprisonment up to 2 years; on indictment: fine up to 200% of tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years. Quebec Tax Administration Act imposes additional fines equal to up to 100% of the evaded duty and daily penalty accruals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner are jointly and severally liable for unremitted taxes and penalties; asset seizure, including personal bank accounts and real estate, may follow; conviction triggers travel bans, disgorgement, and extradition exposure in cross-border schemes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length management fees, inflating intercompany cost bases, or allocating no profit to the Quebec re-invoicing hub despite significant functions, assets, and risks; failing to prepare contemporaneous TP documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may reprice all transactions to arm's length, adjust income upward, and apply a 10% gross-negligence transfer-pricing penalty under s.163(2) on the net understated income; interest is compounded daily and treaty adjustments may be grossed up under s.247(10).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be named on directors' liability certificates and held personally liable for amounts the corporation fails to remit; participation in deliberate mispricing may trigger criminal liability and personal monetary sanctions in civil courts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, interest, or management fees to non-resident partners or affiliates without withholding 25% statutory tax, or without obtaining and retaining treaty relief documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding agent is liable for the full unwithheld amount plus interest and a 10% penalty under s.227(9); Revenu Quebec may impose equivalent obligations under the Quebec Tax Administration Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable under s.227.1 ITA for the corporation's unremitted Part XIII amounts; travel bans may issue, personal assets can be garnished, and director disqualification may be ordered.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Quebec Limited Partnership solely as a pass-through invoice shell with no commercial substance, behind which layering occurs via Swift_LC, TT_Wire, or XT_Transfer rails, and where nominee partners or undisclosed principals control accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PCMLTFA administrative monetary penalties for corporations up to CAD 1,000,000 per violation; Criminal Code s.462.31 money laundering carries imprisonment up to 10 years, asset forfeiture, and court-ordered fines; Canada Border Services Agency and FINTRAC may coordinate asset freezes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in or ignore laundering indicia face personal criminal liability, travel bans, extradition risk, director disqualification, and substantial civil restitution for victims and governmental authorities.
